# X

How far across a position is.

---

Put **x** after a position to read the first of its two numbers, in pixels. **x** grows to the right:
a sprite farther right on the screen has a bigger **x**.

Add **gets** to change just that number. **DO myself position x gets 80** moves your sprite across to
80, keeping its height, and with a position variable named **home**, **DO home x gets 80** changes the
spot **home** remembers. A new position variable starts at **origin**, so you can change its **x**
right away.

Tucked under **WHEN in range**, the rule **WHEN sprite in range position x greater than myself position
x DO move right** follows that sprite to the right while it is farther right than yours.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": ["tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.in-range"],
      "do": [],
      "children": [
        {
          "version": 1,
          "when": [
            "tile.out->struct:<Sprite>.inRange",
            "tile.accessor->struct:<Sprite>->position",
            "tile.accessor->struct:<Vector2>->x",
            "tile.op->gt",
            "tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.myself",
            "tile.accessor->struct:<Sprite>->position",
            "tile.accessor->struct:<Vector2>->x"
          ],
          "do": ["tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.move", "tile.modifier->modifier.direction.right"],
          "children": [],
          "comment": "Head right while the nearby sprite is farther right."
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "catalog": []
}
```

# Y

How far down a position is.

---

Put **y** after a position to read the second of its two numbers, in pixels. **y** grows downward, the
same way **down** points on **move**: a sprite higher up the screen has a smaller **y**.

Add **gets** to change just that number. **DO myself position y gets 20** moves your sprite up or down
to 20 from the top of the screen, keeping how far across it is, and with a position variable named
**home**, **DO home y gets 20** changes the spot **home** remembers. A new position variable starts at
**origin**, so you can change its **y** right away.

Tucked under **WHEN in range**, the rule **WHEN sprite in range position y less than myself position y
DO move up** climbs while that sprite is higher up the screen than yours.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": ["tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.in-range"],
      "do": [],
```

# Position

A spot on the screen, or a direction.

---

A sprite's **position** is the spot its center is at, and **dpad** carries the direction it points as
a position too. A **position** variable remembers one. **origin** is the top-left corner of the screen,
where **x** and **y** are both 0.

## X and Y

`tile:tile.accessor->struct:<Vector2>->x` reads how far across a position is, and
`tile:tile.accessor->struct:<Vector2>->y` how far down, both in pixels, one number at a time.

To change where something is, give it a whole new position with **gets**, or change just one of its
numbers: **DO myself position x gets 80** moves your sprite across to 80, and **DO home y gets 20**
changes the spot a position variable named **home** remembers. Open either to see how.

## Starting From Origin

A position variable starts at **origin**, so you can change its numbers right away: **DO home x gets
80** and **DO home y gets 60**, and **DO move toward home** heads for the spot 80 across and 60 down.
**origin** is a position of its own too: **DO move toward origin** heads for the top-left corner, and
**DO home gets origin** sends **home** back there.

## A Snapshot

A position keeps the spot it was given until a rule changes it. **myself position** is where your
sprite stood the moment it was read: with a position variable named **home**, **WHEN this page starts
DO home gets myself position** remembers where your sprite began, and **DO move toward home** goes back
there later, wherever the sprite has wandered since.

## Working Out New Positions

**plus** adds two positions and **minus** takes one from another, **x** with **x** and **y** with
**y**. A position **multiplied by** a number has both its numbers multiplied by it; the number goes
after the position. Each gives a new position. Positions cannot be divided, and a result too big to
hold is no position at all.

**WHEN in range DO move toward home multiplied by 0.5 plus sprite in range position multiplied by 0.5**
makes a goalkeeper that stands halfway between home and whatever comes near.

Two positions are **equal to** each other when their **x** and their **y** both match.

# Brain

The brain a sprite runs.

---

Put **brain** after a sprite to read the brain it runs, or nothing while it runs none --
`concept:nothing` has the details.

**gets** switches the sprite to another brain from the next frame. Switching it to the brain it already
runs changes nothing; the brain does not start over. **WHEN bump DO bumped sprite brain gets myself
brain** spreads your sprite's brain to whatever it touches.

To stop a sprite's brain, make a brain with no rules and switch the sprite to that one: a brain with no
rules does nothing.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": ["tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.bump"],
      "do": [
        "tile.out->struct:<Sprite>.bumped",
        "tile.accessor->struct:<Sprite>->brain",
        "tile.op->assign",
        "tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.myself",
        "tile.accessor->struct:<Sprite>->brain"
      ],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Spread this brain to whatever this sprite bumps."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": []
}
```

```assistant
- Reading brain gives a Brain value naming the brain the sprite runs now, or nothing while it runs none.
  A brain asked for by a write is not read until it has started, on the next frame.
- A brain write is a request applied at the start of the next frame, ending the brain the sprite ran.
  Writing the brain it already runs does nothing: no restart. Writing a brain the project does not
  hold does nothing.
- The editor never offers nothing as the value a gets writes, so a brain cannot be stopped by writing
  nothing. To stop one, write a brain with no rules.
- Two Brain values are equal to each other when they name the same brain. A Brain value is also the
  filter of bump, in range and out of range, admitting the sprites running it.
- Other sprites' brains are written through the output tiles, as [bumped sprite] [brain] [gets] <brain>.
```

# Move Smoothing

How gradually a sprite speeds up.

---

Put **move smoothing** after a sprite to read how gradually it speeds up, in seconds: its own smoothing,
else the game's, and 0 while its moves start at full speed.

**gets** gives the sprite smoothing of its own: **DO myself move smoothing gets 0.15** eases its starts,
and 0 -- or any number below it -- makes it start crisply even while the rest of the game is smoothed.
Writing anything that is not a number changes nothing.

A brain reads and writes seconds; your game's JavaScript gives the same smoothing in milliseconds, as
`wendoo.moveSmoothing = 150` for the whole game or `wendoo.setMoveSmoothing(mySprite, 150)` for one
sprite.

Smoothing belongs to **move**: it eases how **move** speeds the sprite up. Slowing down and stopping
still happen at once, and a speed your game's own code gives the sprite is not smoothed, though a
**move** eases on from it.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": ["tile.sensor->on-page-entered"],
      "do": [
        "tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.myself",
        "tile.accessor->struct:<Sprite>->moveSmoothing",
        "tile.op->assign",
        "tile.literal->number:<number>->0.15"
      ],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Ease this sprite's moves from the start."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": [
    {
      "version": 2,
      "kind": "literal",
      "tileId": "tile.literal->number:<number>->0.15",
      "valueType": "number:<number>",
      "value": 0.15,
      "valueLabel": "0.15",
      "displayFormat": "default"
    }
  ]
}
```

# Sprite

A sprite in your game, with parts a brain can read and change.

---

**myself**, **bumped sprite**, **sprite in range** and **sprite out of range** each give you a sprite,
and a **sprite** variable holds one. Put a part after a sprite to read it, and add **gets** after the
part to change it: **DO myself image gets bumped sprite image** dresses your sprite like whatever it
bumps.

Two sprites are **equal to** each other when they are the same sprite.

## Image

`tile:tile.accessor->struct:<Sprite>->image` is the picture the sprite wears; **gets** dresses it in
another one.

## Position

`tile:tile.accessor->struct:<Sprite>->position` is where the sprite's center is; **gets** puts it
somewhere else at once.

## Brain

`tile:tile.accessor->struct:<Sprite>->brain` is the brain the sprite runs; **gets** switches it to
another from the next frame.

## Move Smoothing

`tile:tile.accessor->struct:<Sprite>->moveSmoothing` is how gradually the sprite speeds up, in
seconds; **gets** gives it smoothing of its own.

Open a part to see how it reads and changes.

## When a Sprite Is Destroyed

A destroyed sprite reads as nothing: a WHEN holding it does not fire, its parts read nothing, and
changing a part of it changes nothing. `tile:tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.destroy` destroys a sprite,
and `tile:tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.destroyed` lets a sprite's own brain act one last time when it is
destroyed.

# Score

A player's score.

---

Put **score** after a player to read that player's score: **WHEN player one score greater than 9 DO
move** moves your sprite once player one has scored 10. A score is always a whole number.

**add score** adds to it, and **gets** sets it: **DO player one score gets 0** puts player one's score
back to 0.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": [
        "tile.literal->struct:<Player>->1",
        "tile.accessor->struct:<Player>->score",
        "tile.op->gt",
        "tile.literal->number:<number>->9"
      ],
      "do": ["tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.move"],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Move once player one has scored 10."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": [
    {
      "version": 2,
      "kind": "literal",
      "tileId": "tile.literal->number:<number>->9",
      "valueType": "number:<number>",
      "value": 9,
      "valueLabel": "9",
      "displayFormat": "default"
    }
  ]
}
```

```assistant
- [player one] .. [player four] [score] reads that player's score, a whole number, 0 before anything
  changes it. Arcade's own score is player one's: game code's info.setScore and info.changeScoreBy
  change what [player one] [score] reads.
- [player one] .. [player four] [score] [gets] <number> sets that player's score outright, though a
  player tile is a fixed value: the write goes to Arcade's own score. Arcade keeps whole numbers, so a
  fraction is dropped toward zero, and a value holding no finite number changes nothing. [add score]
  adds to a score instead.
- Reading player one's score shows nothing on the screen. Reading or changing the score of player two,
  three or four switches the game to Arcade's display for several players, for the rest of the scene.
```

# Player

One of the four players in your game.

---

**player one**, **player two**, **player three** and **player four** are the players of an Arcade game,
each with a controller of its own. Give one to **dpad**, **A button** or **B button** to read that
player's controller, or to **add score** to change that player's score. Without one, each uses player
one.

A **player** variable holds one, and your game can put a player into it with **set brain player**.

## Score

`tile:tile.accessor->struct:<Player>->score` is a player's score. Put it after a player to read it, and
use **add score** to change it.

Player one's score shows on the screen once it changes. Once a rule reads or changes the score of
player two, three or four, the game shows scores the way Arcade does for several players: each in a
corner of its own.

# Dpad

On while the player holds the dpad, carrying the direction it points.

---

Place **dpad** on the **WHEN** side of a rule to act while the player holds the dpad. The rule carries
the direction the dpad points, so **WHEN dpad DO move** steers your sprite with it.

Add **up**, **down**, **left** or **right** to listen to just those directions. **WHEN dpad left right
DO move** slides your sprite from side to side: held up and to the left, the dpad carries just left,
and held straight up, it is off.

On a controller with an analog stick, a stick pushed part of the way carries a shorter direction, and
**move** goes slower along it.

**dpad** reads player one's dpad. Give it a player to read that player's instead: **WHEN dpad player two
DO move** steers your sprite with player two's controller.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": [
        "tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.dpad",
        "tile.modifier->modifier.direction.left",
        "tile.modifier->modifier.direction.right"
      ],
      "do": ["tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.move"],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Slide from side to side with the dpad."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": []
}
```

## Modifiers & Parameters

| Modifier                                       | Description          |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.direction.up`    | Listen to up         |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.direction.down`  | Listen to down       |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.direction.left`  | Listen to left       |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.direction.right` | Listen to right      |

```assistant
Grammar of dpad, as the editor offers it:
- up, down, left, right: each optional, each at most once, in any order.
- One optional Player, at most once, anywhere among the modifiers: [player one] .. [player four].
  Nothing else: no other value, no parameter, no output tile. dpad is not inline, so no accessor or
  operator follows it and it fills no value slot; its reading reaches the DO side only as the WHEN
  result.

What it reads: the controller of the Player placed, else player one's, fresh at every run, as a Vector2
(x grows rightward, y downward). A Player placed as anything but a literal tile that reads as nothing
leaves the rule off for that frame.
- A digital dpad reads -1, 0 or 1 on each axis, so a held diagonal reads (1, 1) in size, longer than 1.
  Both buttons of one axis held read 0 on that axis; only opposite buttons held reads off.
- An analog stick reads each axis dead-banded: a deflection up to 0.1 reads 0, the rest rescales from 0
  to 1. A stick pushed part of the way reads a vector shorter than 1.

The modifier mask:
- None placed admits every component. Each placed modifier admits only its own direction's component,
  and every other component reads 0. A kept component keeps its size; nothing is rescaled.
- Opposite modifiers do not cancel on dpad: left and right together admit the whole horizontal axis,
  and all four together are the same as none.
- A reading masked to (0, 0) is off. WHEN dpad up is off while only right is held, and carries (0, -1)
  while up and right are held.

The WHEN result is the masked Vector2, and move consumes it:
- An undirected move -- no direction modifier, or move's own modifiers cancelling, and no direction
  value placed after move -- goes along it, held to length 1: a digital diagonal moves at the speed of a
  straight line, and a shorter analog reading moves slower in proportion.
- move's own cardinals, a toward or away from with a target, or wander replace that direction, and dpad
  only gates the rule: WHEN dpad up DO move left goes left while up is held.
- toward or away from with no target placed add nothing under dpad, its result being no Sprite, so the
  move still follows the dpad.
```

# Move

Moves your sprite.

---

Place **move** on the **DO** side of a rule to move your sprite while the rule is on. When no rule
moves it any more, the sprite stops.

Add **up**, **down**, **left** or **right** to pick its direction -- **up** and **right** together move
on the diagonal, as fast as a straight line. Add **toward** or **away from** to chase or flee the
sprite its WHEN carries: **WHEN bump DO move away from** runs from whatever it bumps for as long as
they touch, turning as that sprite moves. Put a sprite after **toward** or **away from** to chase or
flee that sprite instead, like the **sprite in range** a rule above found, or a position to head for
or leave that spot. Add **wander** to stroll from one random spot on the screen to the next.

They all mix with the other directions: **toward** and **up** together chase while drifting upward,
and **toward** with **wander** drifts after a sprite. A move heading for one place -- just **toward**
a sprite or a spot, or just **wander** -- stops right on it instead of going past, and stays put once
it is there.

Without a direction to go, it moves in the direction its WHEN carries -- **WHEN dpad DO move** follows
the dpad -- or rightward when there is none.

Add **slowly** or **quickly** (up to three times) to change its speed, or give it a **speed** in
pixels per second.

| Words on **move**            | Pixels per second         |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| **slowly slowly slowly**     | 12.5                      |
| **slowly slowly**            | 25                        |
| **slowly**                   | 50                        |
| no **slowly** or **quickly** | 100                       |
| **quickly**                  | 200                       |
| **quickly quickly**          | 400                       |
| **quickly quickly quickly**  | 500 -- Arcade's top speed |

500 pixels per second is the fastest an Arcade sprite moves. A move asking for more goes at 500 in
the direction it asks.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": ["tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.bump"],
      "do": ["tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.move", "tile.modifier->modifier.movement.away"],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Run from whatever this sprite bumps."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": []
}
```

## Modifiers & Parameters

| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.direction.up`    | Move up                                                            |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.direction.down`  | Move down                                                          |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.direction.left`  | Move left                                                          |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.direction.right` | Move right                                                         |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.movement.toward` | Chase the sprite the WHEN carries, or the sprite or spot after it  |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.movement.away`   | Flee the sprite the WHEN carries, or the sprite or spot after it   |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.movement.wander` | Stroll from one random spot on the screen to the next              |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.slowly`          | Half the speed. Add up to three                                    |
| `tile:tile.modifier->modifier.quickly`         | Twice the speed. Add up to three                                   |

# In Range

On while the sprite nearest yours is close, carrying that sprite.

---

Place **in range** on the **WHEN** side of a rule to act while another sprite is near yours. It watches
the sprite nearest yours, center to center, and is on while that sprite is within 60 pixels. Give it a
number to pick the range: **in range 40** means within 40 pixels.

**out of range** is its partner. Given the same range, image, sprite or brain, and sides, exactly one
of the two is on whenever there is another sprite to watch, and neither is on while there is none.
**WHEN out of range DO move toward** keeps a companion close, and adding **WHEN in range DO move away
from** makes it hold its distance.

Like **bump**, it can be given an image, a sprite or a brain, to watch only the nearest sprite that
looks like that image, only that sprite, or the nearest sprite running that brain. Add **above** or
**below**, and **left of** or **right of**, to watch only sprites on that side of yours. Your own sprite
never counts.

**in range** looks once a frame, so a fast sprite can jump right across a small range. Keep each range
at least a tenth of the speed of the fastest move in the brain: 10 pixels at the normal speed of 100,
50 at the top speed of 500.

## Sprite In Range

Every time **in range** runs, it puts the sprite it found into `tile:tile.out->struct:<Sprite>.inRange`,
for the rest of the rule and the rules tucked under it to read and change. Open it to see how.

```brain
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Come closer while the nearest sprite is far away."
    },
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": ["tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.in-range"],
      "do": ["tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.move", "tile.modifier->modifier.movement.away"],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Back off while it is close, so this sprite holds its distance."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": []
}
```

# Game Over

Ends the game.

---

Place **game over** on the **DO** side of a rule to end the game the way Arcade does: the game stops,
shows how it ended, and starts again at the next button press. On its own, **game over** ends the game
as a loss. Add **win** to end it as a win, or give it a player to end it with that player winning: **DO
game over player two** says player two won.

Give it an effect and a sound for the ending: **DO game over win hearts power up**. Without them, the
game ends with Arcade's own: confetti and power up for a win, melt and wawawawaa for a loss.

A game ends only once, so the first frame a **game over** rule is on is the one that counts.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": [
        "tile.literal->struct:<Player>->1",
        "tile.accessor->struct:<Player>->score",
        "tile.op->gt",
        "tile.literal->number:<number>->9"
      ],
      "do": [
        "tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.game-over",
        "tile.modifier->modifier.outcome.win",
        "tile.literal->struct:<Effect>->confetti"
      ],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Win with confetti once player one has scored 10."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": [
    {
      "version": 2,
      "kind": "literal",
      "tileId": "tile.literal->number:<number>->9",
      "valueType": "number:<number>",
      "value": 9,
      "valueLabel": "9",
      "displayFormat": "default"
    }
  ]
}
```

```assistant
- In any order, each at most once: an optional [win] or [lose] (one of the two at most), an optional
  Player, an optional Effect and an optional Sound. Nothing else: no named parameter, no output tile.
- No [win] and no Player: the game ends as a loss. [lose] says the same thing.
- [win]: the game ends as a win.
- A Player: that player wins, as Arcade's game.gameOverPlayerWin ends a game. [win] or [lose] beside a
  Player changes nothing: [game over] [lose] [player two] still ends with player two winning.
- An Effect and a Sound are shown and played as the game ends with the outcome this tile gives it; a
  Player winning is a win. Without one, that outcome keeps its own: Arcade's confetti and power up for a
  win, melt and wawawawaa for a loss, unless the game's code set others.
- A Player, Effect or Sound placed as anything but a literal tile that reads as nothing leaves the action
  undone for that frame. An Effect or Sound naming nothing Arcade holds is read as none.

What it does:
- It is Arcade's own game over: the game stops, shows the effect, plays the sound, shows the result and
  restarts at the next button press. When the game's code handles game over itself (game.onGameOver),

- Arcade ends a game once and ignores every later game over, so unlike add score it does NOT act again
  on later frames: the first frame its rule fires decides how the game ends. To compose an ending, give
  it a WHEN that fires at the ending moment, such as [player one] [score] [greater than] 9 or [bump]
  with a filter; when two game over rules fire on the same frame, the one running first wins.
```

Removes a sprite from the game.

---

your own sprite. Give it a sprite to destroy that one instead: **WHEN bump DO destroy bumped sprite**
eats whatever your sprite bumps.

Give it a particle effect to make the sprite vanish in it, and a **duration** for how many seconds the
effect plays: **DO destroy bumped sprite confetti duration 0.5**. Without an effect, the sprite is gone
at once, whatever the duration.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": ["tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.bump"],
      "do": ["tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.destroy", "tile.out->struct:<Sprite>.bumped"],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Eat whatever this sprite bumps."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": []
}
```

```assistant
- In any order, each at most once: an optional Sprite (the target), an optional ParticleEffect, and the
  optional duration parameter, a Number of seconds. Nothing else: no modifier, no output tile.
- No Sprite: it destroys this program's own sprite; [destroy] [myself] does the same. [destroy]
  [bumped sprite] destroys the sprite bump found -- the "eat" rule.
- A ParticleEffect: the sprite vanishes in that effect over duration seconds, or over the effect's own
  length when no duration, or a duration of 0, is given. A duration below 0 reads as 0.
```

```assistant
  another, in the order they were asked for.
- It writes the answer to its answer output, tile.out->boolean:<boolean>.answer, whose own page holds
  its notes.
- The rule goes on once the button that answered the question is let go.
- With no text placed, it asks the rule's WHEN value: a number, a text or a switch, printed as Arcade
  prints them. Any other WHEN value -- a sprite, a position, or nothing -- and empty text ask nothing:
  answer holds nothing, and the rule goes on at once.
```

# Play Sound

Plays one of Arcade's sounds, or one of your songs.

---

Place **play sound** on the **DO** side of a rule and give it a sound: **WHEN bump DO play sound ba
ding**. On its own it plays ba ding. Give it one of your project's songs instead to play that song:
**WHEN A button DO play sound** followed by your song. The rule waits for the sound to end, so a rule
that stays on plays its sound again each time it finishes.

Add **in background** to let the rule go on while the sound plays, or **looping** to play the sound over
and over until a rule says **stop sounds**. Sounds from different rules and sprites play at the same
time.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": ["tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.bump"],
      "do": ["tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.play-sound", "tile.literal->struct:<Sound>->baDing"],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Ding when the sprite bumps something."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": []
}
```

```assistant
Grammar of play sound, as the editor offers it:
- In either order, each at most once: an optional Sound value or Song value -- one of the two, never
  both -- and one of the modifiers [in background] or [looping]. Nothing else: no duration, no volume,
  no Number, no output tile. To play a pitch, use [play tone].
- A Song value is one of the project's own songs, made in the music editor; the editor offers each as a
  literal tile by the song's name. There are no Song variables.
- A Sound placed as anything but a literal tile that reads as nothing -- a Sound variable never set --
  leaves the action undone for that frame. A Sound naming nothing Arcade holds plays nothing, and so
  does a Song whose song the project no longer holds.

What it does:
- Bare, it plays ba ding; given a Song, that song, under the same modifiers as a Sound. Sounds mix:
  plays from other rules, other sprites and other brains sound at the same time, up to the five melodies
  Arcade plays at once.
- With no modifier, the rule holds until the sound ends: a rule under it does not get its turn, and the
  rule cannot fire again until then, so a rule that stays on plays its sound once per completion, never
  once per frame. Other rules and brains keep running meanwhile.
- [in background]: the rule goes on at once. While the copy this same tile last started is still
  playing, the tile starts nothing, so a rule that stays on starts the next copy only after the last
  one ends. Each placed tile keeps its own copy, and so does each sprite running the brain.
- [looping]: the rule goes on at once, and the sound plays over and over until [stop sounds]. While its
  loop runs, the same tile starts nothing more, so a rule that stays on keeps one loop; after [stop
  sounds], its next firing starts the loop again.
- A sound keeps playing after the brain or sprite that started it is gone, and a loop keeps playing
  through Arcade's game-over screen, until [stop sounds] or the game restarts.
```

# Play Tone

Plays a tone at a pitch.

---

Place **play tone** on the **DO** side of a rule and give it a pitch in hertz: **DO play tone 440**
plays an A for half a second. Give it a **duration** in seconds, a **volume** from 0 to 1, and **to**
with a second pitch to slide between them: **DO play tone 440 to 880 for 1** swoops up for a second.

Add a wave -- **sine**, **square**, **sawtooth**, **triangle** or **noise** -- to change how the tone
sounds, and **vibrato**, **tremolo** or **warble** to make it shake. The rule waits for the tone to end,
and **in background** and **looping** work as they do on **play sound**.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": ["tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.button-a"],
      "do": [
        "tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.play-tone",
        "tile.literal->number:<number>->440",
        "tile.parameter->parameter.to",
        "tile.literal->number:<number>->880",
        "tile.parameter->parameter.duration",
        "tile.literal->number:<number>->1"
      ],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Swoop up from 440 to 880 hertz over a second while A is held."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": [
    {
      "version": 2,
      "kind": "literal",
      "tileId": "tile.literal->number:<number>->440",
      "valueType": "number:<number>",
      "value": 440,
      "valueLabel": "440",
      "displayFormat": "default"
    },
    {
      "version": 2,
      "kind": "literal",
      "tileId": "tile.literal->number:<number>->880",
      "valueType": "number:<number>",
      "value": 880,
      "valueLabel": "880",
      "displayFormat": "default"
    },
    {
      "version": 2,
      "kind": "literal",
      "tileId": "tile.literal->number:<number>->1",
      "valueType": "number:<number>",
      "value": 1,
      "valueLabel": "1",
      "displayFormat": "default"
    }
  ]
}
```

```assistant
Grammar of play tone, as the editor offers it:
- In any order, each at most once: an optional Number, the pitch in hertz; the optional parameters [to]
  (a Number, the pitch in hertz to slide to), [duration] (a Number of seconds) and [volume] (a Number
  from 0 to 1); one wave modifier -- [sine], [square], [sawtooth], [triangle] or [noise]; one effect
  modifier -- [vibrato], [tremolo] or [warble]; and one of [in background] or [looping]. A wave, an
  effect and a playback modifier go together; two waves, two effects, or [in background] with [looping]
  do not. No Sound value: to play one of Arcade's sounds, use [play sound].
- [duration] is the shared parameter [say] and [destroy] also take; [play sound] takes none.
- Defaults: pitch 440, duration 0.5 seconds, volume 1, no slide, no effect. A pitch or [to] below 0
  reads as 0, which is silent; a duration below 0 reads as 0; a volume reads as 0 below 0 and as 1
  above 1. A number that is no finite number -- an infinity or not-a-number -- reads as its default,
  [to]'s being no slide.

What it does:
- With nothing but a pitch and a duration, it is Arcade's own plain tone, a sine wave. With [to], a
  wave, an effect or a volume below 1, it is Arcade's sound effect instead: it slides in a straight line
  from the pitch to [to]'s, in the wave (sine when none is given), with the effect, at the volume.
  Arcade plays its sound effects quieter than its plain tone.
- A tone lasting 0 seconds plays nothing, and the rule goes on at once.
- Holding, [in background] and [looping] work as they do on [play sound]: with no modifier the rule
  holds until the tone ends, so a rule that stays on plays once per completion; [in background] goes on
  at once and the same tile starts its next copy only after its last one ends; [looping] repeats the
  tone until [stop sounds]. Tones mix with every other sound.
```

# Stop Sounds

Stops every sound.

---

Place **stop sounds** on the **DO** side of a rule to silence the game: **WHEN B button DO stop
sounds**. It stops what **play sound** and **play tone** are playing and ends every **looping** sound.

## Example

```brain
{
  "ruleJsons": [
    {
      "version": 1,
      "when": ["tile.sensor->sensor.arcade.button-b"],
      "do": ["tile.actuator->actuator.arcade.stop-sounds"],
      "children": [],
      "comment": "Silence every sound when B is pressed."
    }
  ],
  "catalog": []
}
```

```assistant
Grammar of stop sounds, as the editor offers it:
- It takes nothing: no value, no modifier, no parameter.

What it does:
- It is Arcade's own stop all sounds: every melody and tone playing stops, every [looping] sound from
  [play sound] or [play tone] ends, and so do the sounds and songs the game's own code plays.
- It stops what is playing on the frame its rule fires, nothing started later: a rule that keeps firing
  [play sound] [looping] starts its loop again on its next firing.
- A rule waiting on a sound with no modifier goes on once that sound stops: a melody stops at once, a
  tone at the end of its own time.
```
